content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have experience with [product_name] "non lcd" units of [article_no]. I used memory cards to transfer my program and installed them in the [article_no] unit, then powered on. The transfer always worked well. When I noticed a newer [article_no] with the same size and added ethernet, I purchased it and upgraded my [product_name] software. I consulted guides and searched online, but encountered an issue: the new NON-LCD [article_no] would not install my program from the micro-SD card after a power cycle. I managed to transfer the program using the "transfer" function over ethernet in [product_name]. If I change the program, save it as LSC or BIN on the micro-SD, then place it in the newer [article_no] and power cycle, the device does not load the program. I formatted the micro-SD as FAT32 on my Windows 7 PC. I'm likely overlooking a simple step—any advice is welcome. Thanks!
The micro-SD card should contain the program as a ".bin" file. Additionally, only micro-SD cards up to 32 GB, formatted FAT32, are compatible. Other card types such as SDHC will not work.
Have you updated the hardware setting in your program to match the new [article_no]?

Thank you for your advice, [user_name]. Your comment made me retry the process systematically. I confirmed it's an ordinary 2GB micro-SD card formatted to FAT32. This time, I reformatted it, choosing "default allocation unit size" instead of 4096 in the Windows 7 format options—unsure if that makes a difference. I then created a simple program, transferred it over ethernet to the device, and verified installation. After editing the program, I saved it as a BIN file to the micro-SD, stopped the device, powered off, inserted the SD, and powered on. It worked! I repeated this process for several programs, all successful. Notably, as you suggested, I ensured the hardware type matched the new [article_no] and found my previous file was for the older hardware, which caused earlier failures. After updating, SD card transfers at power-on now function as expected. Thanks again.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced issues transferring programs from a micro-SD card to a newer [product_name] unit ([article_no] without display), despite previous success with an older version. The main problem was an incompatible program file and not updating the hardware type in the project. Once the hardware assignment was corrected in the software, micro-SD transfers worked. Proper micro-SD formatting and hardware compatibility are also important factors explained in troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that programs stored on a correctly formatted micro-SD card and created for the right hardware version will automatically transfer to the [product_name] device after power-on, as was the case with earlier models.
